title: biosig-zarr format version 3: shared definitions
description: Definitions that several format version 3 schemas share, transcribed from spec/index.md on the branch draft/3.0.0, which is the definition. This file validates no document on its own.

zarrConventions.description: Zarr convention: the root attribute zarr_conventions.
zarrConventions.$comment: Zarr convention: zarr_conventions MUST be an array that holds exactly one entry whose uuid is the identifier of the biosig-zarr convention (ADR 0004); the array MAY hold entries for other conventions, whose members this text does not constrain.

contains.$comment: Zarr convention: the entry whose uuid is the biosig-zarr identifier.

uuid.$comment: Zarr convention: the identifier of the biosig-zarr convention.

if.$comment: Zarr convention: the condition selects the biosig-zarr entry.

uuid.$comment: Zarr convention: the identifier of the biosig-zarr convention.

then.$comment: Zarr convention: the entry SHOULD have name equal to biosig-zarr, MAY have spec_url, schema_url and description, and MUST NOT have other members. The SHOULD is not checked.

storageType.$comment: Sample resolution: the storage type MUST be one of int16, int32, float32, and float64.

sourceSampleType.description: Sample resolution: the type of a decoded sample in the source.
sourceSampleType.$comment: Sample resolution: int<N> or uint<N> with N from 1 to 64, float32, float64, or n/a when unknown.

sourceAdcBits.description: Sample resolution: the bit depth of the analog-to-digital converter, only when the source states it.

sourceStep.description: Sample resolution: one source digital step in the channel's unit; nonzero; null for a floating point source, or when unknown.

sourceOffset.description: Sample resolution: the physical value of source digital code 0, in the channel's unit.

sourceDigitalRange.description: Sample resolution: the digital minimum and maximum the source declares; null when it declares none.

derivation.description: The derivation list: every step that made a stored sample differ from the source sample, in the order the steps were applied.

anyOf.$comment: The derivation list: each token is one of the tokens of the table. nonfinite_zeroed is left out, because a writer of version 3 MUST NOT store non-finite samples as physical zero; the token exists for tools that describe a version 2 store.
The derivation list: a profile MAY add tokens that contain a colon, such as nemar:sss.

timestampDerivation.description: Timestamped groups, the time array: what was done to the source timestamps; empty when the values are the source's own timestamps shifted to the origin.

items.$comment: Timestamped groups: the tokens of the time array's derivation, clock_synchronized, dejittered, deduced and sorted. Time regularization: timestamp_derivation takes its tokens from the same list.

validIntervals.description: Valid intervals: where a uniform group holds acquired samples. That the first start is 0, that the intervals are sorted, non-empty and non-overlapping, that the last stop is n_samples, and how start follows from source_time relate two values and are not expressed.
validIntervals.$comment: Channel groups: valid_intervals is never empty.

validInterval.$comment: Valid intervals: each entry is an object with the members start, stop and source_time; the table gives them no Presence column, and every entry carries all three, source_time being null when the source does not say.

timeRegularization.description: Time regularization: null when the source declared uniform sampling; otherwise how per-sample timestamps were placed on the grid.

anyOf.$comment: Time regularization: the members of the table; interpolation is CONDITIONAL.

if.$comment: Time regularization: the condition of interpolation, method interpolated.

then.$comment: Time regularization: interpolation is present when method is interpolated.

else.$comment: Time regularization: a CONDITIONAL member is absent when its condition does not hold.

missingValue.description: Missing values: the stored value that means no sample here, encoded as Zarr v3 encodes fill_value for the array's data type, or null when every stored value is data.
missingValue.$comment: Missing values: a declared missing_value MUST be the value the table gives for the array's data type: -32768 for int16, -2147483648 for int32, NaN for float32 and float64.

missingValueRule.description: Missing values: the rules that tie an array's missing_value to its data type and its fill_value. Applied to every signal array: level 0, every view array, and values in a timestamped group.

if.$comment: Missing values: the int16 row of the table.

missing_value.$comment: Missing values: an int16 array declares -32768, or null for an exact copy.

if.$comment: Missing values: the int32 row of the table.

missing_value.$comment: Missing values: an int32 array declares -2147483648, or null for an exact copy.

if.$comment: Missing values: the float32 and float64 row of the table.

missing_value.$comment: Missing values: a floating point array declares NaN; missing_value MAY be null only on an integer array.

if.$comment: Missing values: the condition of the fill value rule, a declared int16 missing value.

fill_value.$comment: Missing values: when missing_value is not null, the array's fill_value MUST equal it.

if.$comment: Missing values: the condition of the fill value rule, a declared int32 missing value.

fill_value.$comment: Missing values: when missing_value is not null, the array's fill_value MUST equal it.

if.$comment: Missing values: the condition of the fill value rule, a declared floating point missing value.

fill_value.$comment: Missing values: when missing_value is not null, the array's fill_value MUST equal it.

channel.description: Channel groups, Channel objects: the members every channel object has, in a uniform or a timestamped group. Each group schema adds the CONDITIONAL members of its kind.
channel.$comment: Channel groups: the REQUIRED rows of the channel object table.

row_index.$comment: Channel groups: the row_index values of a group MUST be the integers 0 to n_channels - 1.

scale.description: Channel groups: a copy of this channel's entry in the scale array of level 0, or of values, which is nonzero.

not.$comment: Level-0 array: one finite, nonzero factor per channel.

if.$comment: Sample resolution: the condition, source_step null.

source_offset.$comment: Sample resolution: source_offset is null when source_step is null.

if.$comment: The derivation list: the condition, the token nonfinite_to_missing.

then.$comment: Channel groups: nonfinite_samples is CONDITIONAL, present when non-finite source samples were stored as missing, which the token nonfinite_to_missing records.

if.$comment: Missing values: the condition, nonfinite_samples present.

usable_for_inference.$comment: Missing values and Channel groups: a channel with any non-finite source sample stored as missing has usable_for_inference false.

shardingIndexed.$comment: Level-0 array: the sharding_indexed codec, with its inner codec chain and its shard index codecs.

name.$comment: Level-0 array: the array MUST use the sharding_indexed codec.

configuration.$comment: Level-0 array: the inner codec chain and the shard index codecs.

codecs.$comment: Level-0 array: the inner chain MUST be bytes with little-endian byte order, then blosc with the zstd compressor.

index_codecs.$comment: Level-0 array: the index codecs MUST be bytes with little-endian byte order, then crc32c.

bytesLittle.$comment: Level-0 array and View pyramid: bytes with little-endian byte order.

bloscZstd.$comment: Level-0 array and View pyramid: blosc with the zstd compressor.

crc32c.$comment: Level-0 array: the crc32c index codec.

name.$comment: Level-0 array: the crc32c index codec.

physicalFormula.$comment: Level-0 array: the literal text physical = digital * scale + offset.

scaleArray.description: Level-0 array: one finite, nonzero factor per channel, indexed by row_index.

not.$comment: Level-0 array: one finite, nonzero factor per channel.

offsetArray.description: Level-0 array: one finite offset per channel, indexed by row_index.

zarrFormat.$comment: Zarr requirements: a store MUST be a Zarr v3 hierarchy and MUST NOT use Zarr version 2 metadata.
